plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, fragrant, ruffled blooms unfold from plump round buds. They fill early-summer gardens with lush, romantic color and a sweet perfume that carries on the breeze.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, including the northern United States, Europe and northern China
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot. Ants often crawl over the buds, though they are not needed to open them.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: This wild rose arches over hedgerows and woodland edges. Its simple, five-petaled flowers look like delicate saucers, and they later give way to bright scarlet hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (late May to July)
plants.location: Hedgerows and scrubland across Europe, including the United Kingdom, and into western Asia
plants.funFact: Dog rose hips are among the richest natural sources of vitamin C. During World War II, Britain gathered them to make rosehip syrup.

plants.name: Sophora microphylla
plants.description: Native New Zealand trees drip with clusters of golden, tubular flowers. In the cool season these blooms draw tūī and bellbirds, which feed on the nectar.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in New Zealand (roughly July to October), with some early flowering in cooler months
plants.funFact: The kōwhai's seeds can float in seawater for long periods. This helped related Sophora species spread across the Southern Hemisphere.
